title: Coefficient bounds ensuring nonarchimedean series substitution and Cauchy products
statement:
Let $K$ be a field with a multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value $|\cdot|:K\to\mathbf R_{\ge0}$, complete for the metric $|x-y|$. Formal series have the coefficient and Cauchy-product convention of [def-weil-formal-power-series]. For $\rho>0$, say $H(T)=\sum_{m\ge0}h_mT^m$ is restricted at $\rho$ if $|h_m|\rho^m\to0$. Its evaluation is $H(x)=\sum_{m\ge0}h_mx^m$ for $|x|\le\rho$.

(1) If $H$ and $J$ are restricted at $\rho$, then their formal Cauchy product is restricted at $\rho$ and $(HJ)(x)=H(x)J(x)$ for every $|x|\le\rho$.

(2) Let $\rho,s>0$, $F(T)=\sum_{n\ge0}a_nT^n$ and $G(T)=\sum_{m\ge1}b_mT^m$. Assume
$$|b_m|\rho^m\longrightarrow0,\qquad \sup_{m\ge1}|b_m|\rho^m\le s,\qquad |a_n|s^n\longrightarrow0.$$
Then the formal composition $F\circ G=\sum_{n\ge0}a_nG(T)^n$ is restricted at $\rho$, $|G(x)|\le s$ and
$$(F\circ G)(x)=F(G(x))\quad(|x|\le\rho).$$
More precisely, for every $|x|\le\rho$ the family
$$\left(a_n\prod_{j=1}^n b_{m_j}x^{m_j}\right)_{n\ge0,\ (m_1,\ldots,m_n)\in\mathbf Z_{\ge1}^{\,n}}$$
is summable in $K$ (meaning that finite subsums converge as finite subsets increase), and may be grouped either by $n$ or by $m_1+\cdots+m_n$. Its terms satisfy
$$\left|a_n\prod_{j=1}^n b_{m_j}x^{m_j}\right|\le |a_n|s^n.$$
For $n=0$ there is one term $a_0$, with empty product $1$ and total degree $0$.

source.place: paragraph 3, justification of evaluating the formal identities; the explicit coefficient-summability criterion is supplied by Q153

proof.text: The norm on the additive group of $K$ is $|\cdot|$; its induced metric is exactly the given complete metric. Thus [lem-wf-ultrametric-family-summability] applies, including for a trivial absolute value. Whenever $H$ is restricted at $\rho$ and $|x|\le\rho$, $|h_mx^m|\le |h_m|\rho^m\to0$, so for every $\epsilon>0$ only finitely many terms exceed $\epsilon$. The criterion gives summability and therefore the stated evaluation $H(x)$. In part (2) put $B_m=|b_m|\rho^m$ for $m\ge1$ and $A_n=|a_n|s^n$ for $n\ge0$. Applying this to $G$ and the bound clause of the same node gives $|G(x)|\le s$, since every $|b_mx^m|\le B_m\le s$. Hence $\sum_n a_nG(x)^n$ is summable as well, since its term norms are at most $A_n\to0$.

source.place: paragraph 3: evaluation convergence and the bound for the inner series

proof.text: For part (1), write $U_i=|h_i|\rho^i$ and $V_j=|j_j|\rho^j$, where $J(T)=\sum_j j_jT^j$. Both sequences tend to zero, so choose $M\ge1$ bounding both (bound the finite initial portions and use an eventual bound of $1$). Given $\epsilon>0$, choose $N$ such that $U_i,V_i<\epsilon/M$ for $i\ge N$. For $k\ge2N$, every pair $i+j=k$ has $i\ge N$ or $j\ge N$, so $U_iV_j<\epsilon$. By [def-weil-formal-power-series], the coefficient $c_k$ of $HJ$ is $\sum_{i+j=k}h_i j_j$. Iterating the strong triangle inequality over this finite sum gives $|c_k|\rho^k\le\max_{i+j=k}U_iV_j<\epsilon$. Thus $HJ$ is restricted at $\rho$.

source.place: paragraph 3: weighted coefficient decay of the Cauchy product

proof.text: Fix $|x|\le\rho$. Step 1 gives summability of $(h_ix^i)_i$ and $(j_jx^j)_j$. Apply [lem-wf-nonarchimedean-summable-products] to these two families: the double family $(h_i j_j x^{i+j})_{i,j\ge0}$ is summable with sum $H(x)J(x)$. Apply [lem-wf-summable-family-regrouping] to $p(i,j)=i+j$. Its degree-$k$ fiber is finite and has sum $c_kx^k$, because its pairs are precisely $(i,k-i)$ for $0\le i\le k$. Here $c_k$ is the coefficient defined in [def-weil-formal-power-series]. Thus the grouped sum is $(HJ)(x)$, proving the evaluation identity.

For part (2), write $\mathcal I=\coprod_{n\ge0}\mathbf Z_{\ge1}^{\,n}$. For $\alpha=(n;m_1,\ldots,m_n)$ put $d(\alpha)=\sum_jm_j$ and $t_\alpha=a_n\prod_jb_{m_j}$, using $d=0$, $t=a_0$ for the unique empty tuple. Repeatedly expanding the coefficient formula of [def-weil-formal-power-series] by finite distributivity shows that the coefficient of $T^k$ in $G^n$ is $\sum_{m_1+\cdots+m_n=k}\prod_jb_{m_j}$: for $n=0$ it is $1$ at $k=0$ and $0$ otherwise; appending one positive index proves the induction step. Since $m_j\ge1$, only $n\le k$ can contribute at $k$, and every $m_j\le k$. Each degree fiber of $\mathcal I$ is therefore finite, and the formal composition has coefficient $c_k=\sum_{d(\alpha)=k}t_\alpha$.

Define the nonnegative weighted bound $W_\alpha=|t_\alpha|\rho^{d(\alpha)}=|a_n|\prod_j B_{m_j}\le A_n$. For every $\epsilon>0$ this family has only finitely many $W_\alpha\ge\epsilon$. Indeed, choose $N\ge1$ so that $A_n<\epsilon$ for $n\ge N$. For each $1\le n<N$ with $a_n\ne0$, choose $M_n$ so that $B_m<\epsilon/(|a_n|s^{n-1})$ for $m\ge M_n$; this uses $s>0$ and $B_m\to0$. If any coordinate of an $n$-tuple is at least $M_n$, then $W_\alpha\le |a_n|s^{n-1}B_{m_j}<\epsilon$. If $a_n=0$ there are no exceptional tuples of that length. The remaining tuples lie in the finite union of the finite boxes $\{1,\ldots,M_n-1\}^n$, together with the one empty tuple. This is a finite-counting estimate, not an assertion that the bound $W_\alpha\le A_n$ alone implies summability.

source.place: paragraph 3: uniform finite-exception estimate from both coefficient hypotheses

proof.text: It follows that $F\circ G$ is restricted at $\rho$. Given $\epsilon>0$, apply step 5 with $\epsilon/2$ and let $D$ exceed the total degrees of all the finitely many exceptional tuples (take $D=1$ when there are none). For $k\ge D$, every tuple of degree $k$ satisfies $W_\alpha<\epsilon/2$. The finite coefficient formula of step 4 and the iterated strong triangle inequality give $|c_k|\rho^k\le\max_{d(\alpha)=k}W_\alpha\le\epsilon/2<\epsilon$; if the fiber is empty its coefficient is zero. This proves weighted coefficient decay without choosing an element of norm $\rho$ or assuming $\rho$ belongs to the value group.

source.place: paragraph 3: restriction of the formal composition on the full closed disc

proof.text: For any $|x|\le\rho$, multiplicativity gives $|t_\alpha x^{d(\alpha)}|\le W_\alpha\le A_n=|a_n|s^n$. The finite-exception estimate of step 5 and [lem-wf-ultrametric-family-summability] show that the family $(t_\alpha x^{d(\alpha)})_{\alpha\in\mathcal I}$ is summable. Use [lem-wf-summable-family-regrouping] first with $d:\mathcal I\to\mathbf Z_{\ge0}$: step 4 identifies the finite degree-fiber sum with $c_kx^k$, so the total sum is $(F\circ G)(x)$. Use the same node with $\alpha\mapsto n$ to group by length; it also guarantees summability on each length fiber and equality with the total sum. This proves both permitted groupings, including the length-zero and degree-zero fiber consisting of $a_0$.

source.place: paragraph 3: summability and the two regroupings of the flattened monomial family

proof.text: To identify the sum grouped by length, fix $x$ and put $q_m=b_mx^m$ for $m\ge1$, a summable family with sum $G(x)$ by step 1. Induct on $n$ to show that the tuple family $(\prod_{j=1}^nq_{m_j})_{(m_1,\ldots,m_n)}$ is summable with sum $G(x)^n$. At $n=0$ this is the singleton family with value $1$. The induction step is [lem-wf-nonarchimedean-summable-products] for the length-$n$ family and $q$; splitting a tuple into its first $n$ entries and its last entry is a bijection, and the nets of finite sums agree under its image map. Applying that node once more with the singleton family of value $a_n$ identifies the length-$n$ sum as $a_nG(x)^n$. Thus step 7 grouped by length is $\sum_n a_nG(x)^n=F(G(x))$, whose summability was proved in step 1. Equality of the two groupings proves $(F\circ G)(x)=F(G(x))$.

source.place: paragraph 3: repeated-product induction identifying the length-grouped sum

split_report.summary: Kept the repaired Q153 statement unchanged. Proved the weighted coefficient decay for products and compositions by explicit finite-exception estimates, including empty tuples. Added three general Mathlib leaves for ultrametric summability/bounds, arbitrary-fiber regrouping, and multiplication of summable families; no clause of the item was moved into a new lemma. Checked pinned source and attachment candidates, formal evaluation hypotheses, and all citation statements.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q53-2a3395d6d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item's statement (the Q153 statement, unchanged), all 8 steps and the 3 new Mathlib leaves in full, plus def-weil-formal-power-series, def-weil-field, the unit sk-d-real-log and blueprint main-20261015 lem-wf-deep-principal-unit-log.proof.md paragraph 3. Step 1: the cofinite criterion gives evaluation, and the bound with C=s>0 gives |G(x)|<=s. Step 2: the M>=1, N, k>=2N estimate on the Cauchy-product coefficient is correct and elementary. Step 3: the product leaf plus regrouping by i+j over finite fibers gives (HJ)(x)=H(x)J(x). Step 4: the induction for the coefficients of G^n is properly set up, and fibers are finite since m_j>=1. Step 5: the finite-exception estimate really uses B_m->0, not only W<=A_n; with B_m constant there would be infinitely many length-1 exceptions. Step 6: composition decay uses no point of norm rho. Steps 7-8: the two regroupings, the induction for G(x)^n via the product leaf and a bijection, and singleton scaling by a_n, all correct. Mathlib sources checked at the lines cited: Nonarchimedean.lean:104 (summable_iff_tendsto_cofinite_zero), :126, :135, :139 (mul_of_nonarchimedean, NonarchimedeanRing section, no completeness needed); Ultra.lean:197 (nonarchimedeanGroup instance) and :347 (norm_tsum_le_of_forall_le_of_nonneg, needs C>=0); Constructions.lean:240 (tsum_fiberwise, needs CompleteSpace and T2); Group.lean:301 (subtype). One caveat: Mathlib has no ready-made NonarchimedeanRing instance for an ultrametric normed field. It is a two-field instance built from Ultra.lean:197, which B8 accepts. I tested the leaves on empty and singleton index sets, empty fibers, a non-surjective p and the trivial absolute value.
